original_statement:
What must hold? State the invariant or expectation this concerns. ArmadaCrowdfund takes the active-window duration as a constructor argument and stores it as an immutable, replacing the 21-day constant. LAUNCH_TEAM_INVITE_PERIOD (currently = WINDOW_DURATION) follows the same immutable. The constructor rejects a zero duration. The production deploy path passes 21 days, and a deploy check rejects any other value for a mainnet config (with a forge or script test of that check). The fixturenet deploy (the arn-d36 governance-stack harness) reads a short window from its config, so deploy -> commit -> finalize -> claim can complete within the 1800s gate. Every caller and test of the constructor is updated.
What holds now? Describe the current, observed state. contracts/crowdfund/ArmadaCrowdfund.sol:76 declares WINDOW_DURATION = 21 days as a constant; :80 LAUNCH_TEAM_INVITE_PERIOD = WINDOW_DURATION (constant); windowEnd (:119) and launchTeamInviteEnd (:120) are immutable, set in the constructor as openTimestamp + the constant; :473 finalize() requires block.timestamp > windowEnd. A real geth+lighthouse fixturenet has no time-travel RPC, so finalize cannot run for 21 real days, which blocks the G7a gate (arn-da4). CLAIM_DEADLINE_DURATION (:81, 3 years) is a constant but an upper bound satisfied immediately at claim, so it is not a blocking wait. Baal votingPeriod/gracePeriod are set at summon (deploy-configurable, so the fixturenet summon can use short values), not contract constants.
How do you see it? Describe exactly how to observe this for yourself — the steps to reproduce, or how you would demo it. On the fixturenet, deploy ArmadaCrowdfund with a short window (e.g. 60s), commit, wait out the short window, finalize, claim -- all within 1800s. Read ArmadaCrowdfund.windowEnd and confirm it equals openTimestamp + the passed duration. Attempt a mainnet-config deploy with a non-21-day duration and confirm the deploy check rejects it. Deploy with a zero duration and confirm the constructor reverts.
What constraints apply? State them in plain prose. Fund-moving Solidity: red-first forge tests. One file at a time (collision lesson). Production deploys MUST pass 21 days; a deploy check enforces 21 days for mainnet configs. The fixturenet short window is config-only, never the production value. Update every caller and test of the ArmadaCrowdfund constructor (deploy_crowdfund.ts, test-foundry, the governance-stack gate scripts).
Where does this apply? (e.g. gateway route, mobile screen, CLI verb) contracts/crowdfund/ArmadaCrowdfund.sol (constructor, WINDOW_DURATION, LAUNCH_TEAM_INVITE_PERIOD); scripts/deploy_crowdfund.ts; test-foundry; env/gates/governance-stack (armada-nitro, after re-pin).

Decomposed child: scripts/deploy_crowdfund.ts (the production deploy path) passes 21 days (1814400 seconds) as the ArmadaCrowdfund window duration constructor argument. A deploy check rejects any window duration other than 21 days for a mainnet config, and the deploy then does not start. A mainnet-config deploy with a non-21-day duration fails with an error that names the window duration. A mainnet-config deploy with exactly 21 days passes the check. A non-mainnet (fixturenet/local) config can pass a shorter duration. The short window is config-only and is never the production value. Add a forge or script test that proves the check rejects a non-21-day value for a mainnet config and accepts 21 days. This part requires the ArmadaCrowdfund constructor to take the window duration as an argument.
restatement: The production crowdfund deploy script, scripts/deploy_crowdfund.ts, must pass a window duration of 21 days (1814400 seconds) to the ArmadaCrowdfund constructor. Before the deploy starts, the script checks the window duration against the target config. For a mainnet config, any value other than 1814400 seconds stops the deploy before it sends a transaction, with an error that names the window duration. For a mainnet config, exactly 1814400 seconds passes the check. For a non-mainnet config (fixturenet or local), a shorter window duration passes the check. A short window is a config value for test networks only and is never the production value. A test proves that the check rejects a non-21-day value and accepts 21 days for a mainnet config. This part depends on a sibling part that changes the ArmadaCrowdfund constructor to take the window duration as an argument.

goal: Make the production crowdfund deploy refuse to start on a mainnet config unless the window duration is exactly 21 days (1814400 seconds), while test networks can use a shorter window.
acceptance_criteria: When asked for the window duration that the production deploy uses for a mainnet config, the deploy script reports 1814400 seconds.
When the window check runs for a mainnet config with a 14-day window (1209600 seconds), it refuses, no deploy starts, and the error message names the window duration.
When the window check runs for a mainnet config with exactly 1814400 seconds, it accepts the value.
When the window check runs for a local config with a 1-hour window (3600 seconds), it accepts the value.
The test for the window check passes, and it fails when any comparison or true/false value in the check is changed.
